skill.name: connector-slack
skill.description: Provides an experimental Motoko recipe for posting messages from Caffeine canisters through Slack's Web API using the pre-release slack-client package.
skill.summary: Build admin-configured Slack messaging into a Caffeine canister.
skill.author: caffeinelabs

security_audit.summary: All 65 external-command alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and code fences; no Ruby or shell backtick execution exists. The three hardcoded URLs point to official Slack properties and match the connector's declared purpose. The example exposes posting to every authenticated caller, enabling unauthorized Slack messages under the configured workspace credential.

remediation.issue: The postSlackMessage example permits every non-anonymous caller to send messages with the shared Slack credential.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit sender permission before posting, restrict allowed channels, validate message limits, and add rate controls.

content.value_statement: Caffeine canisters need secure Slack messaging without custom HTTP and authentication code. This skill provides an experimental client setup, token guidance, and Motoko examples.
actual_capabilities: Chooses between bot and user tokens based on message identity requirements.
Adds slack-client and Caffeine authorization dependencies.
Stores the workspace token behind an administrator permission check.
Configures non-replicated Slack HTTPS outcalls with bearer authentication.
Posts channel messages and returns the Slack message timestamp.
Explains Slack scopes, channel invitations, and current decoding limitations.
limitations: Uses pre-release slack-client version 0.0.3 and is not production-ready.
Success and error response decoding lacks complete runtime verification.
Supports one administrator-supplied workspace token, not per-user OAuth.
Covers selected messaging APIs from an archived Slack specification.

use_cases.title: Add Application Alerts
use_cases.description: Send operational notifications from a Caffeine application to a designated Slack channel.

use_cases.title: Secure Workspace Setup
use_cases.description: Configure a workspace token, minimal scopes, channel membership, and administrator-only secret updates.

use_cases.title: Prototype Slack Workflows
use_cases.description: Test bot or user message identity before committing to a production integration.

prompt_templates.title: Post a Basic Notification
prompt_templates.prompt: Add Slack notifications to my Caffeine canister. Use a bot token and post [message] to [channel]. Explain the required setup.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with one application-owned channel notification.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the Token Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare bot and user tokens for [workflow]. Recommend one, list required Slack scopes, and explain identity and channel access consequences.
prompt_templates.scenario: Select the correct Slack identity and permissions.

prompt_templates.title: Secure Slack Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement administrator-only Slack token configuration and authenticated posting. Restrict senders to [role], allow [channels], and avoid exposing the token.
prompt_templates.scenario: Add explicit application authorization around Slack messaging.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Resilient Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production hardening plan for this experimental connector. Cover authorization, rate limits, retries, response decoding, observability, secret rotation, and tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluate and close gaps before production deployment.

output_examples.input: Post deployment alerts to the engineering channel as the application.
output: Selected a bot token because messages should represent the application.
Invite the Slack app to the engineering channel before testing.

output_examples.input: Allow support leads to send approved incident updates to two Slack channels.
output: Store the token through the administrator-only setter.
Require the support-lead permission before each post.
Allow only the two approved channel identifiers and apply rate limits.

output_examples.input: Assess whether this connector is ready for production.
output_examples.output: The connector remains experimental. Verify response decoding, add sender authorization, test Slack error handling, rotate secrets, and monitor rate limits before production use.

best_practices: Prefer bot tokens unless a workflow explicitly requires a person's Slack identity.
Grant only required Slack scopes and limit posting to approved channels.
Protect token updates and message posting with separate role permissions.
anti_patterns: Do not expose Slack tokens to the frontend, logs, URLs, or generated output.
Do not permit every authenticated caller to post with a shared workspace credential.
Do not present the pre-release connector as production-ready without runtime tests.

faq.question: Which Slack token should I use?
faq.answer: Use a bot token for application messages. Use a user token only when the message must represent a specific person.

faq.question: Which Slack scope is required for posting?
faq.answer: The basic posting flow requires chat:write. Add other scopes only when the selected API method requires them.

faq.question: Must the Slack app join the channel?
faq.answer: A bot must usually be invited to each target channel. User tokens inherit the authorized person's channel access.

faq.question: Does the skill support per-user OAuth?
faq.answer: No. It supports one administrator-supplied bot or user token and does not implement OAuth redirects, exchanges, or refreshes.

faq.question: Is this connector production-ready?
faq.answer: No. Version 0.0.3 is experimental, and success and error response decoding still need complete runtime verification.

faq.question: How should posting access be protected?
faq.answer: Require an explicit application role, restrict allowed channels, validate message size, and apply rate controls before using the shared credential.
